title: NEB Class 11 Mathematics — Algebra — 2020
origin: curated NEB-pattern set filling the 2020 gap for class-11 algebra

questions.solution:
In GP the middle term squared equals the product of neighbours: $x^2 = 2\times8 = 16$, so $x = \pm 4$.
The GP $2, 2\sqrt{2}, 4, \dots$ has $a = 2$, $r = \sqrt{2}$. Sum of $n$ terms: $S_n = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1)$.
$S_6 = 2((\sqrt{2})^6 - 1)/(\sqrt{2}-1) = 2(8-1)/(\sqrt{2}-1) = 14/(\sqrt{2}-1)$. Rationalise: $14(\sqrt{2}+1)/((2-1)) = 14(\sqrt{2}+1)$.
questions.question: If $2, x, 8$ are in geometric progression, find $x$. Then find the sum of the first 6 terms of the GP $2, 2\sqrt{2}, 4, \dots$

questions.solution:
Factorise: $2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 2x^2 - 6x - x + 3 = 2x(x-3) - 1(x-3) = (2x-1)(x-3)$. Roots: $x = 1/2$ and $x = 3$.
Check: sum $= 1/2 + 3 = 7/2 = -b/a = 7/2$ ✓. Product $= (1/2)\times3 = 3/2 = c/a = 3/2$ ✓. Both relations hold, confirming the roots.
questions.question: Solve the quadratic equation $2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0$ by factorisation, and verify the roots using the sum and product of roots.

questions.solution: For a $2\times2$ matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$, $|A| = ad - bc$. Here $|A| = 2\times3 - 1\times0 = 6$.
